gilmoreosaurus:enwiki:4.title: Gilmoreosaurus (Reclassification as Gilmoreosaurus and subsequent research)

facts.statement: The genus Gilmoreosaurus was formally described by Brett-Surman in 1979.
facts.quote: authority: Brett-Surman, 1979

facts.statement: Gilmoreosaurus lived during the Late Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Late Cretaceous,

facts.statement: The type species Gilmoreosaurus mongoliensis is known from the Iren Dabasu Formation in Inner Mongolia and dates to 96 million years ago.
facts.quote: The type species is Gilmoreosaurus mongoliensis, known from the Iren Dabasu Formation of Inner Mongolia, dating to 96 million years ago.

facts.statement: Additional species G. atavus and G. arkhangelskyi have been described from Uzbekistan, but their classification is considered dubious due to fragmentary remains.
facts.quote: Additional specimens have been described as distinct species, including G. atavus from the Khodzhakul Formation of Uzbekistan, and G. arkhangelskyi from the Bissekty Formation, also of Uzbekistan.

facts.statement: The species G. kysylkumense is sometimes included in Gilmoreosaurus but has also been referred to the genus Bactrosaurus.
facts.quote: An additional species, G. kysylkumense, also from the Bissekty Formation, is sometimes included, though it has also been referred to the related genus Bactrosaurus.

facts.statement: Initial excavations of dinosaur fossils at the Iren Dabasu Formation occurred over three days in April and May 1922.
facts.quote: The initial excavations of dinosaur fossils at Iren Dabasu took place on three days in April and May 1922.

facts.statement: More extensive excavations at the Iren Dabasu Formation took place from April 23 to June 1, 1923.
facts.quote: They conducted more extensive digs a year later from April 23 to June 1, 1923.

facts.statement: Gilmoreosaurus fossils were discovered by George Olsen in quarries 145 and 149, located about 14 km northeast of Erenhot, approximately 1 km apart.
facts.quote: The material that would eventually come to be known as Gilmoreosaurus was discovered by George Olsen (a member of Granger's team) in two different quarries (145 and 149, about 1 km apart), around 14 km northeast of the town of Erenhot and not far from the border with Mongolia.

facts.statement: Charles W. Gilmore published his description of Gilmoreosaurus and other dinosaurs in 1933.
facts.quote: He published his findings in 1933, describing both hadrosaurs as well as several other dinosaurs.

facts.statement: The species originally named Mandschurosaurus mongoliensis was later reclassified as the type species Gilmoreosaurus mongoliensis.
facts.quote: The second, known from at least four individuals and thought to be a hadrosaurine, was named as a new species of Mandschurosaurus, M. mongoliensis.

facts.statement: Anatoly K. Rozhdestvensky debated in the 1960s that Bactrosaurus was a hadrosaurine rather than a lambeosaurine.
facts.quote: Anatoly K. Rozhdestvensky, in the 1960s, considered a different solution; that Bactrosaurus was in fact a hadrosaurine, not a lambeosaurine.

facts.statement: Later authors disagreed with Rozhdestvensky, maintaining that Bactrosaurus is a lambeosaur and distinct from hadrosaurines.
facts.quote: Future authors would disagree, reaffirming the two hadrosaurs as distinct and Bactrosaurus as a lambeosaur.

facts.statement: Michael K. Brett-Surman and John R. Horner investigated additional material from Iren Dabasu to better understand the fauna.
facts.quote: Brett-Surman reported that he and John R. Horner were at work investigating this material to form a more complete understanding of the formations' fauna.

facts.statement: Albert Prieto-Márquez and Mark A. Norrel published a thorough redescription of Gilmoreosaurus in 2010.
facts.quote: Albert Prieto-Márquez and Mark A. Norrel began work on a thorough redescription of Gilmoreosaurus; this was published in 2010.

facts.statement: Gilmoreosaurus was a large hadrosauroid reaching lengths of up to 6.2 meters and weights between 1.2 and 3.6 tons.
facts.quote: Gilmoreosaurus was a relatively large-sized hadrosauroid which could grow up to 6.2 m long and obtain weights between 1.2 to 3.6 t.

facts.statement: Specimen AMNH FARB 30729 consists of a left ulna and radius representing a single animal.
facts.quote: the specimen AMNH FARB 30729 represents a single animal composed by a left ulna and radius.

facts.statement: Pascal Godefroit and colleagues argued in 1998 that skull material previously debated belonged to Bactrosaurus rather than Gilmoreosaurus.
facts.quote: The issue would finally be put to rest by Pascal Godefroit and colleagues in 1998, when they published a study describing newly discovered Bactrosaurus material.

facts.statement: Godefroit and colleagues concluded that the skull material belonged to Bactrosaurus, rejecting the idea of two taxa in the quarry.
facts.quote: They returned to the original position of Gilmore, that the possibility of two taxa in the Bactrosaurus type quarry was extremely remote and that the skull material belonged not to Gilmoreosaurus but Bactrosaurus.

facts.statement: Godefroit and colleagues suggested Bactrosaurus was a primitive hadrosauroid that was convergent with later relatives rather than a true hadrosaurid.
facts.quote: The reasoning for the paradoxical nature of the anatomy was that Bactrosaurus was not a lambeosaur or even hadrosaurid at all but instead a more primitive form of hadrosauroid merely convergent with its later relatives.

facts.statement: Brett-Surman described Gilmoreosaurus anatomy as partly iguanodont and partly hadrosaurine, viewing it as an ancestral hadrosaurine form.
facts.quote: He described the anatomy of Gilmoreosaurus as "partly iguanodont and partly hadrosaurine" and saw it as the ancestral form of hadrosaurine

facts.statement: The idea that the two Iren Dabasu hadrosaurs were synonyms was rejected due to numerous differences found between them.
facts.quote: They also specifically touched on the idea the two Iren Dabasu hadrosaurs could be synonyms as Rozhdestvensky had thought. This idea was rejected, with numerous differences between the two found.

facts.statement: No complete articulated skull of Gilmoreosaurus is known, but numerous skull elements including the maxilla, dentary, jugal, squamosal, lacrimals, quadrate, and predentary have been found.
facts.quote: A complete skull articulated is not known from the multiple specimens, however, numerous elements are known such as the right maxilla, dentary, jugal, squamosal and two lacrimals, quadrate and a complete predentary.

facts.statement: Gilmoreosaurus teeth are oval-shaped with a pinched upper end and coarse denticles that possess three diminutive pointed structures.
facts.quote: The teeth are oval-shaped with a moderately pinched upper end and have coarse denticles, these denticles have three diminutive pointed structures.

facts.statement: The total number of dentary teeth in Gilmoreosaurus was probably less than 30.
facts.quote: The total dentary teeth count on Gilmoreosaurus was probably less than 30

facts.statement: A complete predentary from specimen AMNH FARB 6369 has a U-shaped form.
facts.quote: The predentary is represented by a complete element of specimen AMNH FARB 6369, which has a U-shaped form.

facts.statement: The dorsal surface of the Gilmoreosaurus predentary has numerous pointed denticles that create a serrated texture.
facts.quote: Numerous and pointed denticles are preserved on the dorsal surface of the predentary, giving a serrated texture.

facts.statement: The known vertebral column of Gilmoreosaurus includes four cervical, ten dorsal, seven sacral, and thirty-three caudal vertebrae.
facts.quote: The vertebral column is represented by four cervical, ten dorsal, seven sacral and thirty three caudal vertebrae of several specimens.

facts.statement: Neural spines on the anterior dorsal vertebrae are very elongated, subrectangular, and slightly curved to the posterior side.
facts.quote: The neural spines are very elongated and subrectangular in shape, they are slightly curved to the posterior side.

facts.statement: Caudal vertebrae have very flattened centra with small neural canals and neural spines projected towards the rear.
facts.quote: The caudal vertebrae have very flattened centra with smally neural canals and neural spines that are projected towards the rear

facts.statement: The tooth row in Gilmoreosaurus is oriented to the lateral sides, a trait seen in hadrosauroids but lost in more advanced hadrosaurids.
facts.quote: The tooth row is oriented to the lateral sides as seen in other hadrosauroids, unlike the more advanced hadrosaurids.

facts.statement: A ridge-like formation on the posterior edge of the quadrate is reported in other iguanodontians and hadrosauroids like Brachylophosaurus and Gryposaurus.
facts.quote: This character is also reported in other iguanodontians and hadrosauroids, such as Brachylophosaurus or Gryposaurus.

facts.statement: The coracoid bone has an oval shape with a prominent foramen for the supracoracoid nerve, and the glenoid is D-shaped.
facts.quote: The coracoid has an oval-shaped form with a prominent coracoid foramen through which the supracoracoid nerve passes and the glenoid is D-shaped.

facts.statement: The bottom articulation of the coracoid is shortened, triangular, and directed downward, differing from the lateral hooking seen in many other hadrosauroids.
facts.quote: The bottom articulation is shortened and triangular, as well as directed to the bottom area rather than hooked from the rear to the bottom in a lateral as in many other hadrosauroids and not hadrosaurids.

facts.statement: The scapula is very straight when viewed from the top and has a flattened inner surface along most of its length.
facts.quote: The scapula is very straight in a top view with its inner surface being flattened throughout most of the length.

facts.statement: The deltopectoral crest extends from the upper half of the humerus to the lower side, with its bottom extension having a width-to-shaft-diameter ratio of 1.67.
facts.quote: The deltopectoral crest—where the deltoid muscle was attached to the upper front of the humerus—is developed to the lower side from the upper half of the humerus, and its bottom extension has a total width diameter of the humeral shaft ratio of 1.67.

facts.statement: In cross-section, the humeral shaft is elliptical and gently flattened on the lateral surface.
facts.quote: In cross-section, the humeral shaft is elliptical in shape and gently flattened to the lateral surface.

facts.statement: A large tuberosity is located on the posterior surface of the humerus at approximately one-third of the distance from the upper end.
facts.quote: A large tuberosity can be observed on the posterior surface of the humerus—about 1/3 the distance from the upper end.

facts.statement: The ilium is elongated and shallow, with a preacetabular process that is long and deflected toward the bottom.
facts.quote: The ilium is elongated and shallow in shape with its preacetabular process (anterior expansion of the iliac blade) also being long and deflected towards the bottom.

facts.statement: The supraacetabular process has an asymmetrical, V-shaped profile with a lateral projection tilted toward the bottom.
facts.quote: The supraacetabular process (a bony projection at the top border of the ilium) has an asymmetrical, v-shaped appearance in profile and its lateral projection is tilted to the bottom.

facts.statement: The ischium is notoriously elongated and possesses a wide, robust iliac peduncle that connects to the ilium.
facts.quote: The ischium is notoriously elongated and has a wide and robust iliac peduncle—tubercle-like structure that connects to the ilium.

facts.statement: The femur of Gilmoreosaurus possesses a well-developed fourth trochanter and lateral-inner condyles similar to other hadrosauroids.
facts.quote: This element is mostly similar in build to other hadrosauroids with a well-developed fourth trochanter and lateral-inner condyles.

facts.statement: The fossil collection of Gilmoreosaurus includes about six tibia elements.
facts.quote: One of the most common elements among the collection is represented by the tibia—about six elements.

facts.statement: The tibia of Gilmoreosaurus is a robust element slightly shorter than the femur with a cylindrical shaft expanded at both ends.
facts.quote: It is a robust element that is slightly shorter than the femur, and is composed of a rather cylindrical shaft that is expanded at both upper and lower ends; more expanded at the latter though.

facts.statement: The tibia of Gilmoreosaurus features a very elongated and developed cnemial crest near its upper end.
facts.quote: The cnemial crest is very elongated and developed near the upper end of the bone.

facts.statement: The bottom tilt of the lateral malleolus distinguishes adult from juvenile tibiae in Gilmoreosaurus, being less developed in juveniles.
facts.quote: A main difference between the juvenile and adult tibiae can be noted by the bottom tilt of the lateral malleolus—this trait is less developed in juveniles.

facts.statement: The fibula of Gilmoreosaurus is particularly straight and elongated.
facts.quote: The fibula is particularly straight and elongated.

facts.statement: The astragalus is the largest tarsal element in Gilmoreosaurus.
facts.quote: Among the tarsal elements, the astragalus is the largest.

facts.statement: Metatarsals III and IV are present in the foot of Gilmoreosaurus.
facts.quote: Among the metatarsus elements, metatarsal III and IV are present.

facts.statement: The pedal unguals of Gilmoreosaurus are more arrow-shaped and sharply developed than those in hadrosaurids.
facts.quote: These elements are more arrow-shaped and more sharply developed than in hadrosaurids.

facts.statement: Gilmoreosaurus had a light constitution for its size of around seven meters, with well-developed hind limbs allowing for a fast run.
facts.quote: Era de constitución ligera para su tamaño de alrededor de siete metros de largo, con miembros posteriores bien desarrollados que le permitirían una rápida carrera.

facts.statement: The claw-like feet of Gilmoreosaurus resembled those of iguanodontids like Iguanodon more than those of hadrosaurids.
facts.quote: Sus pies con aspecto de garra se parecían más a las de un iguanodóntido, como el Iguanodon, que a las de un hadrosáurido.

facts.statement: The mouth of Gilmoreosaurus was filled with small teeth that were replaced as they wore down, similar to later hadrosaurids.
facts.quote: Su boca está repleta de pequeños dientes que se remplazaban a medida que se desgastaban, como en hadrosáuridos posteriores.

facts.statement: The first fossil remains of Gilmoreosaurus were collected by George Olsen in 1923, consisting of disarticulated bones from several individuals.
facts.quote: Los primeros restos fósiles de Gilmoreosaurus fueron recolectados por George Olsen en 1923, los cuales consistían en huesos desarticulados de varios individuos en diferentes localidades.

facts.statement: The type species was originally described as Mandschurosaurus mongoliensis in 1923 and renamed Gilmoreosaurus mongoliensis in 1979 based on remains from the 70-million-year-old Iren Dabasu Formation in Mongolia.
facts.quote: La especie tipo fue descripta como Mandschurosaurus mongoliensis en 1923 fue renombrada en 1979 con el nombre actual Gilmoreosaurus mongoliensis, a partir de restos encontrados en Mongolia, de la formación Iren Dabasu, que data de 70 millones de años.

facts.statement: The species Gilmoreosaurus atavus was described in 1995 by Nessov from the Khodzhakul Formation in Uzbekistan, and Gilmoreosaurus arkhangelskyi from the Bissekty Formation dates to 89 million years ago.
facts.quote: Una nueva especie Gilmoreosaurus atavus se conoció en 1995 por Nessov de la formación Khodzhakul de Uzbekistán, datada hace millones de años, Gilmoreosaurus arkhangelskyi de la formación Bissekty, hace 89 millones de años.

facts.statement: The classification of Gilmoreosaurus atavus and Gilmoreosaurus arkhangelskyi is doubtful because they are based on very fragmentary remains.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, estos se basan en restos muy fragmentarios, y su clasificación es dudosa.

facts.statement: The genus Gilmoreosaurus was established by Brett-Surman in 1979.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Brett-Surman, 1979

facts.statement: The type species of Gilmoreosaurus is Gilmoreosaurus mongoliensis.
facts.quote: type_species: Gilmoreosaurus mongoliensis

facts.statement: Gilmoreosaurus belongs to the family Hadrosauroidea.
facts.quote: familia: Hadrosauroidea

facts.statement: Gilmoreosaurus lived during the Early to Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Cretácico Inferior-Superior

facts.statement: Gilmoreosaurus lived from the Aptian to Campanian stages of the Middle to Late Cretaceous, approximately 120 to 70 million years ago, in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: Gilmoreosaurus (“lagarto de Gilmore”) es un género representado por 4 especies de dinosaurios ornitópodos hadrosauroides que vivieron de mediados a finales del período Cretácico desde el Aptiense al Campaniense, hace aproximadamente entre 120 a 70 millones de años en lo que es hoy Asia.

facts.statement: The bottom tilt of the lateral malleolus is a trait used to distinguish juvenile from adult tibiae in Gilmoreosaurus.
facts.quote: A main difference between the juvenile and adult tibiae can be noted by the bottom tilt of the lateral malleolus—this trait is less developed in juveniles.

facts.statement: Many consider Gilmoreosaurus one of the most primitive hadrosaurids, characterized by large lower jaws, long hind legs, and the absence of a hollow crest.
facts.quote: Es considerado por muchos como uno de los hadrosáuridos más primitivos, tenían grandes las mandíbulas inferiores y las patas traseras largas y no tenían la cresta hueca.

facts.statement: The species Gilmoreosaurus kysylkumensis is sometimes included in Gilmoreosaurus but has also been referred to the related genus Bactrosaurus.
facts.quote: Una especie adicional , Gilmoreosaurus kysylkumensis, también de la formación Bissekty, se incluye a veces, aunque también se ha referido al género relacionado Bactrosaurus.

facts.statement: A 2010 study by Prieto-Márquez and Norell places Gilmoreosaurus in a clade closely related to Hadrosauridae based on phylogenetic analysis.
facts.quote: un estudio de 2010 realizado por Prieto-Márquez y Norell coloca al animal en un grupo externo estrechamente relacionado con Hadrosauridae

facts.statement: Gilmoreosaurus belongs to the parent group Hadrosauroidea.
facts.quote: Parent group: Hadrosauroidea

facts.statement: Gilmoreosaurus is classified in the class Ornithischia.
facts.quote: Class: Ornithischia

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Gilmoreosaurus is Gilmoreosaurus mongoliensis.
facts.quote: Type species: Gilmoreosaurus mongoliensis

facts.statement: Gilmoreosaurus lived during the Campanian stage, between 83.6 and 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: In 2003, evidence of tumors including hemangiomas, desmoplastic fibroma, metastatic cancer, and osteoma was discovered in fossilized Gilmoreosaurus skeletons.
facts.quote: En 2003, se descubrió evidencia de tumores, incluidos hemangiomas, fibroma desmoplásico, cáncer metastásico y osteoma en esqueletos de Gilmoreosaurus fosilizados

facts.statement: Rothschild and colleagues studied dinosaur vertebrae for tumors using computed tomography and fluoroscopy detection.
facts.quote: Rothschild et al. estudiaron vértebras de dinosaurios buscando tumores mediante tomografía computarizada y detección con fluoroscopio

facts.statement: Although more than 10,000 fossils were examined this way, tumors were found only in Gilmoreosaurus and closely related genera.
facts.quote: Aunque se examinaron más de 10000 fósiles de esta manera, los tumores se limitaron a Gilmoreosaurus y géneros estrechamente relacionados

facts.statement: It is debated whether the tumors found in Gilmoreosaurus were caused by environmental factors or genetic predisposition.
facts.quote: Los tumores pueden haber sido causados por factores ambientales o por propensión genética
